name: DG Matrix Inc. (Delaware corporation; SEC CIK 0002059108; North Carolina registration formed 10 November 2022 per state-record mirror)
headquarters: 951 Aviation Parkway, Suite 1000, Morrisville, North Carolina, United States (Raleigh–Durham); SEC Form D business address Cary, NC; earlier releases datelined Raleigh
employees: '250+ engineers' (company About page, 2026); 'about 400 engineers today' (CEO, MCJ podcast, May 2026); 185 total employees per a PitchBook snippet (aggregator); engineering and an operating factory in Lahore, Pakistan reported by engage.vc (November 2025) — not on the current company site
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: DG Matrix is the third venture-backed solid-state-transformer startup at the AI hall edge and the only one shipping a product — but the product shipping is a six-port low-voltage skid (Interport Flex, 200 and 400 kVA, 480 V AC in, 800 V DC out, 96–97% peak efficiency on its own datasheet), not the 12–34.5 kV medium-voltage unit that competes with Heron Power and Amperesand, which the company's own roadmap dates to '2028+'. As of 19 September 2026 it has USD 60M of Series A capital (February 2026, Engine Ventures; ABB and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries on the cap table), an Infineon silicon-carbide supply agreement, a self-declared NVIDIA MGX ecosystem membership that no NVIDIA-published roster corroborates, 'pre-certification units … shipping' against a UL target that passed at the end of Q2 2026 without an announced listing, and no named, energised commercial customer site on the public record. BACKGROUND. Founded 2022 in Raleigh, North Carolina by CEO Haroon Inam (ex-CTO of Smart Wires) and CTO Dr. Subhashish Bhattacharya (NC State; FREEDM Systems Center solid-state-transformer research since 2008), DG Matrix began as a multi-port EV fast-charging company (Natron sodium-ion partnership, December 2023; FlexGen EMS, August 2024), branded its unit the 'Power Router' and re-pointed it at data centers through 2025, then relaunched as 'Interport' with the Series A in February 2026. Three product tiers: Interport Flex (six-port LV skid, 'commercially deployed'; paralleled into 'Interport 360'), Interport Cell-LV (three-port sidecar for GPU pulse loads, ±400 / 800 V DC), and Interport Cell-MV (three-port medium-voltage SST skid, 'up to 15 MW UPS power', 2028+). Funding per company releases: USD 20M seed (March 2025, Clean Energy Ventures; ABB minority stake via ABB Electrification Ventures), USD 60M Series A (18 February 2026), 'over $100 million' total, which Power Electronics News breaks down as USD 80M equity, USD 15M venture debt and USD 10M loans. Partners: PowerSecure (Southern Company) as nationwide channel, Exowatt, Ampace, Skeleton Technologies, InfraPartners, Satterfield & Pontikes. Collection gap: no datasheet exists for either Cell Series, no topology, cell count or switching frequency is disclosed, no factory capacity or opening date is published, the Form D amounts cannot be read (sec.gov blocked), and every shipped-unit statement is the company's own.
ecosystemRole: We assess DG Matrix as the low-voltage-first challenger in the hall-edge power-conversion layer — a multi-port converter that today replaces the transformer-rectifier-UPS chain at 480 V behind the meter and in the gray space, sold against conventional microgrid and UPS packages now and positioned against Heron Power, Amperesand and the hedged incumbents (ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Siemens, Schneider, Delta) for the 34.5 kV-to-800 V DC block once its Cell-MV exists. Its adjacency to in-hall power is the Cell-LV sidecar, which puts isolation, storage and pulse-load buffering next to the rack — the 'built-in UPS functionality' the company sells against the UPS. It is not a battery, switchgear or rack power-shelf vendor.

productsAndServices.name: Interport Cell-MV Series — medium-voltage multi-port solid-state transformer skid (formerly 'Power Bridge MV SST'; 'Interport CM')
productsAndServices.description: The company's medium-voltage product: 'a three-port, cell-based, medium-voltage solid-state transformer that integrates utility power, onsite generation, and energy storage directly onto a DC backbone' (Grid-to-Rack whitepaper, February 2026). It 'accepts a single MV input port, consistent with utility and MV-generator interconnection practices, while simultaneously integrating battery energy storage and low-voltage AC sources through its additional ports' (Facility Power Fabric whitepaper); the data-center page describes the 'MV – Skid Solution' as 'Interport Cell Series that will transform medium voltage AC (12 – 34.5 kV) to high voltage DC', and the Skeleton release calls it 'the Interport CM medium-voltage SST skid, which converts 12 34.5 kV AC directly to high-voltage DC'. The December 2025 whitepaper rates it 'up to 15 MW UPS power with up to 2x surge', handling 'MV AC (up to 34.5 kV) and DC (300-1,500 V) voltage ranges in single device', for 'gray space or outdoor deployment'. Platform-level claims apply: 'single-stage, multi-port power conversion architecture', 'up to 98.5%' conversion efficiency with Infineon silicon-carbide MOSFETs (March 2026 release), 'galvanic isolation at each port', and ports 'reprogrammable' from ±400 VDC to 'up to 1,500 VDC'. No datasheet exists for the Cell-MV; the CFO's March 2026 roadmap deck places the multi-port medium-voltage SST at '2028+'.
highlights: This is the product that competes with Heron Link and Amperesand's SST at the 34.5 kV-to-800 V DC hall edge — and it is the one DG Matrix has not yet shipped: the December 2025 whitepaper tags only the Flex Series 'Commercially deployed', the March 2026 Infineon release says there is 'now … a clear pathway to multi-megawatt medium voltage solid-state transformers', and the CFO's own deck dates the multi-port MV SST to '2028+' (company documents; the gap between the '15 MW' marketing rating and the roadmap is the dossier's central finding).

The 'end goal is achieving 34.5kV AC to 800V DC power conversion' (CEO, June 2026 Insights post); the whitepapers describe the Cell-MV feeding a DC backbone from which the Cell-LV sidecar regulates ±400 VDC or 800 VDC at the rack.

No first-party statement of dimensions, weight, cell count, cooling, standards targets or lead time exists for the Cell-MV; the only medium-voltage figures on the record are the 12–34.5 kV input range, the '15 MW UPS power' rating and the '2x surge' claim (collection gap).

The medium-voltage lineage is the CTO's: SemiAnalysis, as quoted by the company, 'traces the company's origin to NC State including its FREEDM Systems Center, where the CTO of DG Matrix has been researching solid-state transformers and silicon-carbide transistors since 2008'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Sits at the medium-voltage-to-800 V DC hall-edge block that NVIDIA's August 2026 execution paper builds first from transformer-rectifier units and reserves for 34.5 kV-direct SSTs 'toward 2029' — which is consistent with DG Matrix's own '2028+' date for the multi-port MV SST. The named peer set at this layer is Heron Power (34.5 kV, 4.2 MW single unit, mass production late 2027, on NVIDIA's facility-tier roster) and Amperesand (3.3 kV SiC, 200 kW modules to 4–10 MW, Reno line), plus the hedged incumbents (GE Vernova, ABB, Eaton via Resilient Power, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, Schneider) and Delta, which has a live SST at a Chinese operator. DG Matrix's differentiators, as the record supports them: a multi-port topology (one MV port plus battery and LV AC ports in the same unit, versus the single-input, single-output units of Heron and Amperesand), a shipping low-voltage product family that accumulates field hours before the MV unit exists, ABB and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries on the cap table, an NVIDIA MGX ecosystem listing, and Infineon as named SiC supplier. Its handicap is the same as its rivals' — no certified, energised medium-voltage unit — plus a later MV date than either (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to hyperscale, neocloud and colocation operators and their design-build firms (Satterfield & Pontikes 'priority access', May 2026; InfraPartners RapidNode integration, May 2026), with PowerSecure (Southern Company) as 'nationwide energy partner' for channels, deployment and service (December 2025). No EPC, OEM-merchant or distributor pricing model is published.
targetSegments: AI factories on NVIDIA MGX / 800 V DC racks — hyperscalers, neoclouds and colocation operators
Behind-the-meter power blocks combining utility interconnection, on-site generation and storage (Exowatt, PowerSecure)
Gray-space and outdoor skid deployments at data-center campuses
productsAndServices.roadmap: '2028+: Medium voltage … Multi-port' SST (CFO deck, March 2026); 'clear pathway to multi-megawatt medium voltage solid-state transformers' after the 200 kW and 400 kW Interport launch (Infineon release, March 2026); 'UL certification targeted for the end of Q2 2026' for the Interport platform (June 2026 MGX release — no completion announced as of 19 September 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Interport Cell-LV Series — three-port low-voltage sidecar for GPU pulse loads (formerly 'Power SideCar LV SST'; 'Interport CL' / 'IPT-CL')
productsAndServices.category: In-hall power conversion and pulse-load buffering (white space)
productsAndServices.description: 'A three-port, low-voltage, cell-based platform that converts incoming power and delivers regulated ±400 VDC or 800-VDC output while providing localized energy storage, capacitance, and fast transient support for white-space loads' (Grid-to-Rack whitepaper, February 2026). It 'supports AC input, a dedicated capacitive-module input for AI pulse loading, and regulated ±400-VDC or 800-VDC output, all within a galvanically isolated' unit (Facility Power Fabric whitepaper); the data-center page's 'SideCar Solution' is 'Interport Cell Series designed to be located next to the IT load to address pulse-load mitigation with galvanic isolation'. Rated 'up to 1.6 MW UPS power with up to 2x surge' with 'sub-millisecond surge response at the load interface' (Stranded Power whitepaper). The May 2026 MGX release adds 'integrated liquid cooling, and rack-proximate battery storage for dynamic GPU pulse-load response', and the Skeleton Technologies collaboration (July 2026) integrates GrapheneCBU800/BBU800 supercapacitor storage 'directly in the white space'. The Infineon release names the Cell-LV as one of the two systems using Infineon SiC MOSFETs.
highlights: The sidecar is DG Matrix's answer to the rack-power question NVIDIA's 800 V DC papers pose — pulse-load smoothing next to the IT load — and it is the product tied most directly to the NVIDIA relationship: 'a yearlong program of testing energy storage solutions for dynamic GPU load response in collaboration with NVIDIA' (May 2026 release).

Status: the December 2025 whitepaper carries no 'commercially deployed' tag for the Cell-LV; the May 2026 release speaks of 'the commercial launch of its Interport and Interport Cell products'; no datasheet, dimensions, cooling detail or standards target is published (collection gap).

Programmable output — 'data centers … initially operate at ±400 VDC and reprogram the port to up to 1,500 VDC in the future, supporting with NVIDIA 800 VDC power architecture and Open Compute Project's Mount Diablo guidelines' (December 2025 whitepaper).
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with the DC-side storage and power-shelf layer that Delta, LITEON, Megmeet and Vicor own on NVIDIA's rosters and with the sidecar/BBU designs those vendors showed at OCP 2025, and with DC-coupled battery approaches such as Dimaag's; unlike a power shelf it sits between the facility bus and the rack with its own isolation and storage port. No competitor is named by the company (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, as part of an Interport 360 'grid-to-rack' block with the Flex and Cell-MV; storage partners (Ampace UL-certified BESS, Skeleton supercapacitors, Musashi, Noon Energy, Exowatt) supply the storage side.
targetSegments: GPU white space at 800 V DC (NVIDIA MGX racks; Vera Rubin class)
Retrofits of AC halls to ±400 VDC / 800 VDC distribution
productsAndServices.roadmap: '2026+: Low voltage multi-port SST' (CFO deck, March 2026); Skeleton supercapacitor integration announced July 2026 with no delivery date.

productsAndServices.name: Interport Flex Series — six-port low-voltage multi-port SST skid, 200 kVA and 400 kVA (formerly 'Power Router'), paralleled into 'Interport 360'
productsAndServices.category: Behind-the-meter power routing, microgrid and UPS-class conversion (low voltage)
productsAndServices.description: The shipping product. 'A modular, six-port-capable power routing platform designed to aggregate and distribute AC and DC energy sources within a unified AC/DC architecture. Each unit provides a configurable set of power ports that can be defined at deployment' (Grid-to-Rack whitepaper). Two datasheets exist: the 400 kVA (Rev C) — DC port 300–850 VDC (800 V nominal) at 530 ADC, AC port 400–480 VAC three-phase at 520 A, 50/60 Hz, peak efficiency 96–97%, six ports (standard three AC and three DC), 8,818 lb / 4,000 kg, 51 × 69 × 122 in, liquid cooled (sealed), NEMA 3R, 'Designed for Compliance to* UL 1741' — and the 200 kVA (Rev B) — 350–800 VDC at 250 ADC, 400–480 VAC at 260 A, 96% peak efficiency, six ports (two AC and four DC), 4,409 lb / 2,000 kg, 'Designed for Compliance to* UL 1741, UL 2202, UL 2231'. 'Each port is galvanically isolated and independently controlled, enabling fault-tolerant operation and port-level redundancy. Additional systems can be paralleled to achieve N+1 or greater redundancy' (Behind-the-Meter whitepaper); the December 2025 whitepaper rates a Flex system at 'up to 1.2 MW UPS power' and tags it 'Commercially deployed'. Paralleled Flex skids with the company's energy-management software form 'Interport 360', 'a software-configurable power architecture that supports native AC and DC distribution, 800-VDC readiness, integrated behind-the-meter energy, and AI pulse-load management' (InfraPartners whitepaper, May 2026). The 2025 CEC filing lists the platform's grid functions: 'Native support for black start, islanding, UPS, grid-forming operation, Volt-VAR control, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) integration'.
highlights: The datasheet efficiency is 96–97% peak, not the '98.5%' of the platform claim — the only rating table on the record is two to three points below the headline figure, and the datasheets carry '*Certification information can be provided upon request' rather than a listing.

Six software-defined ports are the multi-port idea made concrete: a 400 kVA unit ships with three AC and three DC ports as standard, and 'Field-reconfigurable AC and DC ports allow migration toward hybrid or fully DC-native architectures'.

This is the unit behind every deployment statement on the record — 'commercial units shipping' (Darcy, March 2026), 'DG Matrix has installed a working pilot at Exowatt' (June 2026), 'Pre-certification units are shipping now' (June 2026) — and the unit Exowatt selected as 'a preferred platform for power conversion' (February 2026).

Ratings and enclosure are datasheet facts: 100 dBA at 1 m (400 kVA) and 75 dBA (200 kVA); −25 to 40 °C operating (the 200 kVA 'is designed to operate at –40 °C; however, for certification purposes, the specified operating temperature range is limited to –25 °C'); 'The footprint does not include the AC and DC switchgear'.

Grid functions per the CEC filing: 'Six bi-directional, software-defined ports that are remotely programmable'; 'Interconnection and commissioning in 1–7 days'; 'currently proven in behind-the-meter applications'.
productsAndServices.positioning: In the behind-the-meter block it replaces the low-voltage transformer, switchgear, UPS, rectifiers and inverters of a microgrid or fleet depot — the company's '10-20 electrical systems' / 'up to 15 discrete electrical components into four' claim — and competes with conventional PCS-plus-transformer microgrid packages from the PowerSecure/Schneider/Eaton class and with grid-forming PCS vendors. In the data hall it is the gray-space, outdoor skid that InfraPartners' RapidNode prefabricated blocks pair with. It is not a medium-voltage product: it connects at 400–480 VAC, so a site still needs the utility transformer the Cell-MV is meant to remove (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales ('sales@dgmatrix.com'; 'Talk to sales'), with PowerSecure as nationwide channel and service partner, general contractors (Satterfield & Pontikes) and modular-data-center integrators (InfraPartners) as design-in partners; FlexGen's HybridOS as EMS partner for fleet charging (August 2024).
targetSegments: Data-center gray space and outdoor skids (paralleled to megawatt blocks; 'Interport 360')
Behind-the-meter microgrids for enterprise and industrial sites (PowerSecure channel)
Fleet-electrification depots and EV charging hubs (with the Interport Dispenser)
Utility and virtual-power-plant edge nodes (Duke Energy award; CEC front-of-meter proposal)
productsAndServices.roadmap: 'commercial launch of its 200 kW and 400 kW Interport units' (Infineon release, March 2026); UL certification 'targeted for the end of Q2 2026' (June 2026); Morrisville manufacturing 'from first unit to hundreds per year' (job postings, September 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Interport Dispenser and fleet-charging configuration (Natron sodium-ion and FlexGen partnerships; the company's 2023–2024 origin market)
productsAndServices.category: EV fleet charging (DC fast-charging dispensers on the multi-port platform)
productsAndServices.description: 'A simple dispenser that works with Interport out of the box' (fleet page), paired with the Flex Series in an 'EV Charging + Microgrid Solution' with '>1-kW dynamic power sharing across ports' and support for 'evolving high-power charging standards (CCS, MCS, DC architectures)'. The company began here: in December 2023 it described itself as 'the global leader in high-power, high-efficiency multi-port electric vehicle (EV) chargers', announced Natron Energy sodium-ion 'Blue Pack' batteries in its fast chargers with 'up to 10-X reduction in product footprint and volume' and said it was 'accepting orders now for delivery in 2024'; FlexGen's HybridOS was added as EMS for EV fleet charging in August 2024. The 2025 CEC filing lists 'Modular and scalable AC or DC Fast Charging with 400 kW capacity' and pilots 'already … demonstrated in behind-the-meter microgrids and EV infrastructure pilots'. The 200 kVA Flex datasheet's UL 2202 and UL 2231 targets mark it as the charging variant.
highlights: No dispenser specification, connector type, power rating or customer is published (collection gap); the fleet market has been de-emphasised on the company's channels since the February 2026 relaunch put data centers first.

The charging heritage matters technically: a fleet depot is where a multi-port unit's dynamic power sharing between ports was first exercised, and where its early field hours were accumulated (analysis).
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with the conventional depot chain (transformer, switchgear, per-charger rectifiers) and with integrated charging-plus-storage vendors; Amperesand pursues the same market at medium voltage for ports (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through fleet-charging developers (anonymised 'Major Fleet Charging Hub Developer' testimonial); FlexGen EMS partnership.
targetSegments: Fleet depots (school bus, delivery, autonomous fleets)
Charging hub developers and utilities' fleet programmes

recentDevelopments.headline: Daniel Doimo (MGE UPS Systems co-founder, ex-Schneider Electric EVP Power, partner at Series A investor Helios) joins the Executive Advisory Board as the company 'accelerates pilot deployments … with hyperscale, neocloud and colocation customers'
recentDevelopments.read: Seven months after the Series A the company's own wording is still 'pilot deployments', and the newest hire advises on 'manufacturing scale-up' — the ramp is ahead, not behind (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA, Google and Microsoft publish the 800 V DC execution paper and note the OCP LVDC Solid-State Transformer Specification v0.3 with 'more than 80 equipment manufacturers'; DG Matrix is not named, and NVIDIA's own SST phase 'targets 2029'
recentDevelopments.read: NVIDIA's public SST timing (2029) is closer to DG Matrix's '2028+' Cell-MV date than to any startup's 2026–2027 promise — the medium-voltage race is later than the funding rounds imply.

recentDevelopments.headline: Skeleton Technologies supercapacitor collaboration across all three tiers — first public naming of the 'Interport CM medium-voltage SST skid, which converts 12 34.5 kV AC directly to high-voltage DC', the 'Interport CL sidecar' and the paralleled Flex 'Interport 360'
recentDevelopments.read: The clearest company statement of the product ladder; the MV skid is described in the present tense while the roadmap deck dates it to 2028+.

recentDevelopments.headline: Deepak Thakkar, Ph.D. (Intel, Flex, Boyd, ECI, Neos Partners) appointed Chief Commercial Officer; release restates 'up to 15 discrete electrical components into four', TCO 'one-half to two-thirds' and deployment 'approximately six months'
recentDevelopments.read: A contract-manufacturing and data-center sales profile in the top commercial seat signals the hyperscale channel is the priority over the fleet and microgrid markets the company came from (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: 'DG Matrix Joins the NVIDIA MGX Ecosystem' as an SST supplier for 800 V DC — 'more than two years of direct technical collaboration with NVIDIA'; 'Pre-certification units are shipping now, with UL certification targeted for the end of Q2 2026'; same day Anthony Wanger named first Executive Chairman and Peter Gross joins the advisory board
recentDevelopments.read: The membership is the company's statement; no nvidia.com page, blog or GTC press-kit item names DG Matrix as of September 2026, and the UL date in the same paragraph has passed without an announced listing.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Interport SST for the NVIDIA MGX Ecosystem' reveal (shown at GTC 2026 in March): 'natively supports 800 VDC today', ports 'up to 1,500 VDC', 'up to 98.5 percent conversion efficiency, integrated liquid cooling, and rack-proximate battery storage', 'a yearlong program of testing energy storage solutions for dynamic GPU load response in collaboration with NVIDIA'
recentDevelopments.read: The NVIDIA collaboration on the record is storage-response testing and rack-interface validation, not a roster listing — a real technical relationship short of the badge the company implies (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: InfraPartners RapidNode prefabricated data center integrated with 'Interport 360'; joint whitepaper cites 'a recent 50 MW client deployment' with 5–10% power-infrastructure capex reduction and time-to-revenue '3–6 months faster'
recentDevelopments.read: The only deployment-scale figure on the record is a modelled client case in a partner whitepaper, not a commissioned site.

recentDevelopments.headline: SemiAnalysis '800VDC Revolution' places DG Matrix as the 'LV-input SST in place of the conventional rectifier-plus-PSU stack', 'ABB-backed', 'shipping pre-certification units and targeting UL certification by end of Q2 2026', 'claims up to 98.5%'; Power Electronics News the same day describes Interport 360 as eight paralleled 400 kVA Flex units (3.2 MVA, 'scalable to 10 MVA') and relays a '10 GW capacity planned online by Q2 2027'
recentDevelopments.read: The independent analyst's word is 'claims', and its classification — low-voltage input — is the distinction that matters against Heron and Amperesand.

recentDevelopments.headline: Satterfield & Pontikes (ENR Top 400 general contractor) gets 'priority access' to Interport for Texas data-center builds, '6 to 9 months' ahead of conventional transformer procurement
recentDevelopments.read: A general contractor as channel is how a startup without a hyperscaler contract reaches the build schedule; the release names no project.

recentDevelopments.headline: Power Electronics News: CTO says 'DG Matrix's current design does not plan to integrate 10 kV devices'; first-generation SSTs run '98–98.5% efficiency—not yet matching conventional transformers' >99%' and cost 'double the price of a normal transformer'
recentDevelopments.read: The medium-voltage unit will be built from lower-voltage SiC in series — the cascaded-cell route its rivals also take — and the efficiency parity claim against iron does not hold on the CTO's own numbers.

recentDevelopments.headline: Heatmap transformer-startups feature transposes the rounds — 'DG Matrix raised a $140 million Series B round and Heron Power raised a $60 million Series A' — with no correction; CEO quoted on a 'multi-billion dollar pipeline'
recentDevelopments.read: Chesterton check for every future refresh: DG Matrix's round is the USD 60M Series A; Heatmap's own February piece and TechCrunch have it right.

recentDevelopments.headline: Infineon named 'a key silicon carbide supplier': latest-generation SiC MOSFETs in the Interport and Interport Cell-LV systems, 'platform efficiencies of up to 98.5%', 'commercial launch of its 200 kW and 400 kW Interport units. Now there's a clear pathway to multi-megawatt medium voltage solid-state transformers'
recentDevelopments.read: The silicon partner's own release dates the medium-voltage product as a 'pathway' after the LV launch — consistent with the CFO's 2028+ slide.

recentDevelopments.headline: Power Electronics News' GTC 2026 roundup lists 'Delta Electronics, DG Matrix, ABB, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, GE Vernova, Eaton (through Resilient Power Systems), Heron Power' as SST providers citing 'Nvidia's list', and quotes the CTO that NVIDIA is 'incorporating it as the reference architecture for 800V DC'
recentDevelopments.read: The only document placing DG Matrix on an NVIDIA roster is this article; every NVIDIA-published list (May 2025, October 2025, August 2026) omits it — treat the roster claim as trade press, not NVIDIA.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rainer Stiller, former Vertiv CMO (2021–2024) and two decades at Schneider Electric/APC, appointed Chief Marketing Officer
recentDevelopments.read: The relaunch team is drawn from the UPS incumbents the product is meant to displace.

recentDevelopments.headline: CEO to Power Electronics News: 'we are currently the only solid-state transformer company shipping a commercial product today'; funding 'over $100 million, including $80 million in equity raised, $15 million in venture debt, and $10 million in loans and debt'
recentDevelopments.read: The only breakdown of the '>$100M' total on the record — a fifth of it is debt — and the sole-shipper claim is the CEO's, repeated by no customer.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 60M oversubscribed Series A led by Engine Ventures with Helios Climate Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Fine Structure Ventures, MCJ and Sabancı Climate Ventures; 'All existing investors committed new capital in this round, including ABB'; total 'over $100 million'; 'multiple gigawatt-class datacenters in the pipeline'; TechCrunch: 'Rolling out initial units June 2026', pipeline '~90% data centers'
recentDevelopments.read: The round that rebranded Power Router as Interport and dated the first production units to June 2026 — a date no source has confirmed met.

recentDevelopments.headline: Exowatt selects the Power Router 'as a preferred platform for power conversion for its modular energy architectures'; a Miami pilot is the first installed data-center-adjacent site the CEO names
recentDevelopments.read: The first named platform customer is a behind-the-meter generation startup, not a hyperscaler — the multi-port unit's natural first buyer is whoever has several sources to blend (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: PowerSecure (Southern Company subsidiary, 'over 3 gigawatts of microgrid capacity') becomes 'nationwide energy partner' — 'immediate customer channels, deployment capacity, and service coverage for our Power Router platform'; a PowerSecure site in Durham is a test location
recentDevelopments.read: A utility-owned microgrid integrator as channel and service arm is the most bankable commercial relationship on the record.

recentDevelopments.headline: Ampace partnership: 'industry's first UL-certified, grid-active Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a multi-port solid-state transformer (SST) platform' — Ampace 'selected DG Matrix after a comprehensive evaluation of competing solutions'
recentDevelopments.read: The UL certification in the headline is the battery's, not the SST's; the partner's endorsement is the strongest third-party product judgment on the record.

recentDevelopments.headline: Power Electronics News founder interview publishes the fullest technical description on record: 'Merged two-stage design' eliminating the DC-link capacitor, switching at 'tens of kilohertz', four 200 kW DC ports plus two 200 kW AC ports, '380-480V AC inputs; future plans extend to 13.8-34.5 kV', patented vortex liquid cooling with '4°C delta' across transistors, '200 kW and 400 kW systems currently shipping; 1+ MW sidecar in development (Q3 2026)'
recentDevelopments.read: The nearest thing to a design disclosure is an interview; the sidecar date it gives (Q3 2026) is the next one to check.

recentDevelopments.headline: Canary Media feature: testing 'with ABB, Duke Energy, and PowerSecure'; North Carolina factory 'opening late 2025' with capacity 'up to 1,000 units annually'; Power Router 'can cost half as much as using the standard mix of multiple technologies'
recentDevelopments.read: The factory date slipped: job postings in September 2026 still describe a Morrisville plant before its 'first production build' (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: California Energy Commission EPIC docket comment by DG Matrix: the Power Router is 'currently proven in behind-the-meter applications' with 'Six bi-directional, software-defined ports', '96–98% system efficiency', 'Interconnection and commissioning in 1–7 days'; asks for front-of-meter demonstration funding
recentDevelopments.read: The company's own regulatory filing scopes what is proven — behind-the-meter, low-voltage — more modestly than its marketing.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 20M oversubscribed seed led by Clean Energy Ventures with ABB, Cerberus Ventures, Chevron Technology Ventures and Piedmont Capital ('nearly $30 million' total); ABB's own release: 'a minority stake … through ABB Electrification Ventures'; 'paid pilot deployments in Q1 2025, with a full commercial launch anticipated in late Q2 2025'; Vlatko Vlatkovic (ex-CTO GE Power Conversion) to the board
recentDevelopments.read: ABB's investment is documented from ABB's side, which is rare for this corpus; the commercial-launch date it announced slipped by at least a year.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that DG Matrix's shipping product is a low-voltage converter and that its medium-voltage SST — the unit that competes with Heron Link and Amperesand's platform — does not yet exist as a product. Basis: the two datasheets (400–480 V AC input, 800 V DC output), the CEC filing ('currently proven in behind-the-meter applications'), SemiAnalysis's 'LV-input' classification, the Infineon release's 'clear pathway to multi-megawatt medium voltage' and the CFO deck's '2028+' for the multi-port MV SST. The 'first company shipping a commercial multiport SST' claim is true of a 480 V unit and does not transfer to the hall-edge block.

(High confidence) We assess that no NVIDIA-published roster names DG Matrix. Basis: the May 2025 and October 2025 developer blogs, the October 2025 and August 2026 corporate blogs and the GTC 2026 press kit, all read in full; the only source placing it on 'Nvidia's list' is Power Electronics News' GTC coverage, and the MGX membership rests on the company's releases and analyst repeats. The technical collaboration (storage-response testing, rack-interface validation) is plausible and unrefuted; the badge is unverified. Collection gap: NVIDIA's MGX partner directory does not render partner names.

(High confidence) We assess that every delivery and certification date has slipped: commercial launch 'late Q2 2025' (March 2025), 'shipping … next month' (Axios, December 2025), 'initial units June 2026' (TechCrunch, February 2026), UL certification 'end of Q2 2026' (June 2026) — and as of 19 September 2026 the company's own wording is 'pilot deployments', the Morrisville plant's job postings precede its 'first production build', and no listing has been announced. Basis: the dated releases and job postings above.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the multi-port topology is a genuine architectural difference, not marketing: one converter with several galvanically isolated, software-defined AC and DC ports lets a site blend utility, generator, battery and solar and serve AC and DC loads from one box, which is what Exowatt, PowerSecure and a fleet depot buy and what a single-input hall-edge SST cannot do. Basis: the datasheets' 3 AC + 3 DC port configuration, the CEC filing's black-start/islanding/V2G functions, the Ampace and Exowatt selections. The cost is that a multi-port LV design is optimised for behind-the-meter aggregation, not for the highest-efficiency single path from 34.5 kV to the rack, where NVIDIA rates the TRU at 98.5% and the company's own datasheet says 96–97% (analysis).

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the company's efficiency and cost claims should be read at the datasheet, not the headline: 'up to 98.5%' (platform), '96–98%' (CEC and trade press), '96–97% peak' (400 kVA sheet), 96% (200 kVA sheet); 'half the cost' (Canary), '60–70% of the cost' (CEO to TechCrunch), TCO 'one-half to two-thirds' (release), 'up to 90% lower system cost' (MCJ). No customer has published a delivered cost or measured efficiency; the CTO's own statement that first-generation SSTs are 'not yet matching conventional transformers' >99%' is the honest baseline.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that roughly USD 80M of equity plus USD 25M of debt funds the Morrisville ramp to 'hundreds per year' of LV units and the Cell-LV sidecar, but not a medium-voltage production line: the peers raised more for less (Heron USD 140M Series B for one 4.2 MW unit; Amperesand USD 80M plus USD 30M), and DG Matrix's MV product is two years out on its own slide. A Series B or a strategic (ABB, MHI, Infineon) manufacturing arrangement before the Cell-MV ships is the expected tripwire (analysis).

(Low confidence) We assess that the reported Lahore, Pakistan engineering and manufacturing footprint (engage.vc, November 2025; '250 engineers') and imported sub-assemblies (Morrisville inventory postings) make domestic-content, FEOC and Section 232 questions live for a US data-center buyer, and that the company has published nothing on them. No source states how Interport is classified for tariff purposes or where its power stages are built; the reading rests on one profile and job postings.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — Q4 2026: any UL 1741 (or UL 2877) listing or NRTL announcement for the Flex 200/400 (converts 'pre-certification' into a bankable product; a second slip past year-end would mean two years late against the March 2025 plan). A named, dated, energised customer site with unit counts — Exowatt Miami, PowerSecure Durham or a hyperscaler pilot — from either party (confirms Judgment 1's 'only one shipping'). The '1+ MW sidecar' (Cell-LV) delivery promised for Q3 2026 (tests the NVIDIA-adjacent product). Any nvidia.com page naming DG Matrix, or its name in the OCP LVDC SST specification contributor list (closes Judgment 2). A Cell-MV datasheet, cell count or kV rating (settles whether the 2028+ unit is a cascaded-cell design and what it competes with). Morrisville 'first production build' and any NC incentive filing with jobs and capex (the only externally checkable ramp numbers). A Series B or strategic manufacturing partnership (tests Judgment 6). ABB and MHI: any first-party statement beyond the seed release, and whether MHI's stake channels through Mitsubishi Power (not on the record).

policyExposure.regime: UL 1741 / UL 2877 / IEEE 1547 certification for power-conversion equipment
policyExposure.exposure: Both Interport Flex datasheets state 'Designed for Compliance to* UL 1741' (the 200 kVA adds UL 2202 and UL 2231, the EV-charging standards) with the footnote '*Certification information can be provided upon request'; no listing appears on any company channel. The June 2026 MGX release said 'Pre-certification units are shipping now, with UL certification targeted for the end of Q2 2026', and SemiAnalysis (May 2026) recorded the same target; no completion had been announced by 19 September 2026. UL 2877 — which applies to power-conversion equipment with input above 1,000 V up to 38 kV — would govern the Cell-MV; no company document names it. The Series A use of funds includes 'advancing UL, IEEE, and international certifications'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Chief Delivery Officer Karamjit Singh, a former Intertek executive with '25+ years driving testing, certification, quality assurance, and compliance programs', per the company's About page; the Ampace partnership pairs the SST with a UL-certified BESS.

policyExposure.regime: Section 232 tariffs on transformers and grid equipment
policyExposure.exposure: Steel-and-aluminium derivative duties were extended to transformers, cores and laminations at 50% on component value from 18 August 2025 (CRS R48933; tEDmag) and restructured by the 2 April 2026 proclamation (effective 6 April; Federal Register 9 April 2026) that caps 'electrical grid equipment' at 15% through 2027 on full customs value. No source addresses how a solid-state transformer — a power-electronics cabinet with a medium-frequency transformer and SiC modules — is classified, and DG Matrix has published nothing on tariff exposure, country of origin or domestic content. Morrisville inventory postings coordinate 'all international inbound shipments — customs documentation' for 'sub-assembly' stock, and engage.vc (November 2025) reports an operating factory in Lahore, Pakistan — so imported content is on the record while its share is not (collection gap).

policyExposure.regime: FEOC / domestic-content and Buy-American expectations for AI-campus procurement
policyExposure.exposure: No FEOC, domestic-content, 45X or Buy-American statement exists for DG Matrix. The company markets Morrisville manufacturing ('new manufacturing facility in Morrisville, NC'; 'scale from first unit to hundreds per year'), while engage.vc reports 'Operating factories in Lahore, Pakistan (250 engineers) and developing one in Raleigh' and the current About page no longer mentions Lahore. Silicon carbide is sourced from Infineon (Germany/Austria/Malaysia fabs). For a hyperscaler or utility buyer applying domestic-content scoring, the record does not say where the power stages, magnetics and enclosures are built (collection gap).

policyExposure.regime: FERC large-load interconnection orders and Texas SB 6
policyExposure.exposure: The company's July 2026 whitepaper argues FERC's large-load orders (a 60-day process) favour behind-the-meter, flexible-load architectures and that Interport 'qualifies for the new service models FERC is asking operators to create'; the Satterfield & Pontikes release cites Texas SB 6 (June 2025) large-load rules as the context for Texas data-center builds.
